evals.prompt: /env-setup scan this Node/Express repo and generate a .env.example
assertions: Greps the codebase for actual environment variable usage before listing any variable names
Only lists variables that were actually found via grep, does not invent plausible-sounding ones
Groups discovered variables by service/prefix (e.g. Database, Auth, Stripe) in the generated .env.example
Generated .env.example contains only placeholder values, never a real secret value
Reads any existing .env.example first and preserves its existing entries/comments rather than overwriting them

evals.prompt: /env-setup validate — check if my .env has everything it needs
assertions: Reads the existing .env file before reporting any findings
Reports variables required by code (no default/fallback) that are missing from .env
Flags empty values (VAR= with no value) for required variables
Checks .gitignore for .env / .env.local entries and warns clearly if .env is not gitignored
Reports stale variables present in .env but not found anywhere in the codebase scan

evals.prompt: In this sandbox repo, first plant these three fixtures, then run /env-setup scan --check-secrets because I'm worried we leaked an API key at some point: (1) create a .env file containing a line `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_abc_123_XYZ` — a secret containing underscores, like most real key formats; (2) `git add .env && git commit -m 'wip'` that same .env, then `git rm --cached .env` and commit again so the secret is gone from the working tree but still present in git history; (3) add a line `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_SECRET=some_value` to .env so a client-exposed variable's name suggests a secret. After planting all three, run the secret-detection scan and report findings.
assertions: Scans .env using a character class that matches underscores/hyphens/dots (not just base64 [a-zA-Z0-9+/]), and actually catches the STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_abc_123_XYZ line
Checks git history (git log --all --full-history) and reports that a .env with a secret was previously committed and later removed
Flags NEXT_PUBLIC_API_SECRET as a client-exposure risk because its name suggests a secret
Report names each finding by variable and file:line (or commit) location only
The report text does not contain the literal string sk_live_abc_123_XYZ anywhere, in chat output or any file written
Recommends a pre-commit secret-scanning tool (e.g. detect-secrets or gitleaks) rather than claiming to be a full security audit

evals.prompt: /env-setup validate — I don't think I even have a .env file yet, check anyway
assertions: Checks for the existence of .env before validating, and clearly reports that no .env file exists rather than fabricating variable values
Does not create, write, or auto-generate a .env file with guessed or placeholder values — no mutating file-write command is run
Still reports which variables the code requires (from the grep scan) so the user knows what to create
Final message tells the user to create .env (e.g. by copying .env.example) and stops there instead of proceeding as if one exists
